ontology_definition: An oxygen preference in which growth can occur without oxygen but is capable of aerobic growth.
taxonomic_resolution: NCBI species/genus isolates; propagated to BugSigDB taxa via NCBI hierarchy
approved_wording: Taxa annotated as facultatively aerobic (capable of growth in both the presence and absence of oxygen).
unsupported_interpretations: Do not infer anaerobic respiration using nitrate or tetrathionate. Do not infer specific respiratory electron transport chains (e.g., nar, nap, ttr). Do not infer mucosal inflammation or host-derived oxidant availability.

ontology_definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of cellulose, a linear beta1-4 glucan of molecular mass 50-400 kDa with the pyranose units in the -4C1 conformation.
taxonomic_resolution: NCBI species/genus isolates; propagated to BugSigDB taxa via NCBI hierarchy
approved_wording: Taxa annotated with pathway capability for cellulose catabolic processes.
unsupported_interpretations: Do not infer demonstrated in vivo cellulose degradation in patients. Do not equate cellulose catabolism with butyrate or short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production (end-products frequently comprise acetate, succinate, lactate, or ethanol).

ontology_definition: A cell shape in which an organism has a spherical or nearly spherical morphology, with roughly equal dimensions in all directions.
taxonomic_resolution: NCBI species/genus isolates; propagated to BugSigDB taxa via NCBI hierarchy
approved_wording: Taxa annotated with coccus-shaped cell morphology (primarily derived from Madin et al. isolate compilation).
unsupported_interpretations: Do not merge with sphere-shaped by naive string rewriting or profile summation. Do not claim biological non-equivalence without noting that differences reflect source database curation boundaries (Madin et al. vs Bactotraits).

ontology_definition: A cell shape defined in METPO as a subclass of cell shape (METPO:1000666); unpopulated narrative definition in KG nodes (synonyms: S_sphere, sphere-shaped).
taxonomic_resolution: NCBI species/genus isolates; propagated to BugSigDB taxa via NCBI hierarchy
approved_wording: Taxa annotated with sphere-shaped cell morphology (derived from Bactotraits and BacDive morphology records).
unsupported_interpretations: Do not treat as a biologically distinct morphology from coccus shaped. Do not sum profile counts with coccus shaped without deduplicating shared taxa.

ontology_definition: Pathway annotation in KG-Microbe for microbial reduction of arsenate; lacks narrative definition in KG nodes; mapped under METPO:2000103 (capable of).
taxonomic_resolution: NCBI species isolates; propagated to BugSigDB taxa via NCBI hierarchy
evidence_status: unresolved mechanism (0/51 KG edges resolve gene or pathway mechanism; unstratified mixture of arrAB dissimilatory respiration and arsC detoxification) + propagated (taxonomic rollup)
approved_wording: Taxa annotated with pathway capability for arsenate reduction (derived from Madin et al. isolate compilation; mechanism unresolved between dissimilatory respiration and cytoplasmic detoxification).
unsupported_interpretations: Do not classify as arsC detoxification. Do not classify as arrAB dissimilatory respiration. Do not infer gene presence, plasmid carriage, patient arsenic exposure, or antimicrobial co-selection from this taxon-level pathway label.

ontology_definition: A halophily preference where growth and proliferation requires high levels of sodium chloride, usually above or about 0.2 M.
taxonomic_resolution: NCBI species/genus isolates; propagated to BugSigDB taxa via NCBI hierarchy
evidence_status: measured (qualitative halophily category in Madin et al.) + unresolved (missing quantitative salt concentration, optimum, range, medium, and culture conditions) + propagated (taxonomic rollup)
approved_wording: Taxa annotated as moderately halophilic (defined in METPO as requiring high levels of sodium chloride, typically above or about 0.2 M NaCl).
unsupported_interpretations: Do not read as 'halotolerant' (halophily requires salt for growth, whereas halotolerance permits growth without requiring salt). Do not claim specific quantitative salt ranges, growth media, or culture conditions from KG edges.
